problem: In monsoon humidity, sieve cloth in the plansifter blinds and fine stock sticks to the wires.
agitation: Sifting capacity drops and stock moves to the wrong stream. Flour passes slowly, the operator keeps adjusting, and the whole flow becomes unstable.
solution_steps: Check that sieve cleaners (balls or brushes) are present, clean and in good condition.
Check the moisture and temperature of the stock reaching the plansifter.
Inspect sieve cloth tension and clean or replace blinded sections.
hook_ideas: Monsoon is blinding your sieves
Damp stock, sticky sieves, falling flow
product_angle: Mention sieve cleaners and spare sieve cloth as items to stock before the rainy season.

problem: Rubber sleeves between plansifter compartments crack and harden in summer heat and start leaking stock.
agitation: Stock leaks between channels and mixes with finer or coarser streams. Floor dust increases and cleaning work grows.
solution_steps: Check all sleeves for cracks, hardening and loose clamps.
Check that sleeve length and diameter match the inlet and outlet properly.
Replace the full set together so they age evenly.
hook_ideas: Summer heat is cracking your sleeves
Small sleeve leaks, big sifting problems
product_angle: Suggest keeping a ready set of sleeves as routine spares for the plansifter.

problem: Sieve frames swell and warp after monsoon moisture, so they no longer sit tightly in the stack.
agitation: Gaps appear between frames and flour escapes or bypasses the sieve. Stock quality varies from shift to shift and the cause is hard to find.
solution_steps: Check frames for warping, gaps and swollen edges when the stack is opened.
Check the sealing strips and gaskets between frames.
Replace damaged frames and keep spares stored in a dry place.
hook_ideas: Swollen frames let flour bypass the sieve
After monsoon, check every frame edge
product_angle: Talk about frames and sealing strips as parts that need a post-monsoon check.

problem: During the harvest rush, a mill patches the plansifter with mixed sieve cloth because the right size was not in stock.
agitation: Uneven sifting follows and stock splits do not match the flow sheet. Millers blame the rolls when the real cause is in the sifter.
solution_steps: Compare each installed cloth with the original flow sheet requirement.
Mark and record which sections have temporary cloth fitted.
Replace temporary sieves with the correct ones as soon as possible.
hook_ideas: Temporary sieve cloth becomes a permanent problem
Wrong cloth, wrong split, lower flour quality
product_angle: Mention that having the correct cloth in stock before harvest avoids make-do fitting.

problem: New-crop wheat brings heavier bran flow and the old plansifter in an older mill is overloaded on the top sieves.
agitation: Bran-rich stock piles up and does not clear. Flour yield suffers and the sifter runs hot and noisy.
solution_steps: Check the sieve cloth openings and condition on the top sections.
Check whether cleaners are working to keep the sieve surface open.
Review the feed to the sifter before changing any other machine.
hook_ideas: New wheat, heavier bran, overloaded sifter
Is your old sifter coping this harvest?
product_angle: Position upgraded sieve cloth and cleaners as a first practical step for old mills.

problem: Humid weather makes semolina stick to purifier sieve cloth and block the openings.
agitation: Air does not pass evenly through the deck and separation becomes poor. Good stock goes to the wrong stream and the operator keeps changing settings.
solution_steps: Inspect the sieve cloth for blinded areas and clean them.
Check that the cleaning brushes or elements are working.
Check the moisture level of the incoming stock.
hook_ideas: Sticky semolina is choking your purifier
Monsoon blinds purifier sieves quietly
product_angle: Introduce purifier sieve cloth and cleaning elements as a seasonal preparation item.

problem: Air flow across the purifier deck is uneven because of loose cloth and worn sealing strips.
agitation: Some areas lift too much and others too little. Separation becomes inconsistent and the miller loses confidence in the machine.
solution_steps: Check cloth tension across the full deck width.
Check side and end sealing strips for gaps and wear.
Check the air adjustment settings after fixing the leaks.
hook_ideas: Uneven air means uneven purification
Loose cloth, leaking seals, poor separation
product_angle: Mention sealing strips and cloth as simple parts that restore even air distribution.

problem: A small mill runs its purifier with worn cleaning brushes because they were never listed as a routine spare.
agitation: The deck clogs a little more every week and the operator accepts the drop in performance. Over time, the stock quality drifts and no one knows why.
solution_steps: Check the condition and contact of the brushes under the deck.
Add brushes to the regular spares list with a change interval.
Record purifier performance after each replacement.
hook_ideas: Worn brushes quietly reduce purifier performance
Brushes are small, but their absence is costly
product_angle: Suggest small mills keep brushes as a low-cost routine spare.

problem: After a purifier sieve change, the new frame does not fit properly and stock leaks along the edges.
agitation: Stock bypasses the cloth and contaminates the cleaner streams. Mill staff lose time re-fitting and re-adjusting during production.
solution_steps: Measure the frame and compare it with the new sieve before ordering.
Check the seating surface for wear or damage.
Fit and test the sieve at low load before full production.
hook_ideas: A sieve that almost fits still leaks
Match the frame before you order cloth
product_angle: Mention that giving machine details or a sample helps match the right sieve and frame.

problem: Rubber hangers and supports in an older purifier harden in summer heat and the deck movement changes.
agitation: The deck vibrates unevenly and stock travels differently across the sieve. Noise rises and parts loosen faster.
solution_steps: Inspect hangers, springs or supports for hardening and cracks.
Check that the deck moves evenly and without knocking.
Replace worn supports as a complete set.
hook_ideas: Hardened supports change how your purifier moves
Summer heat ages purifier supports fast
product_angle: Mention supports and hangers alongside cloth as parts for a pre-season check.

problem: Jet filter bags absorb moisture in monsoon and the dust cake sticks to the cloth.
agitation: Pressure across the filter rises and suction weakens through the mill. Dust escapes at machine points and the floor stays dirty.
solution_steps: Check the bags for damp, caked dust on the outside surface.
Check the pulse cleaning cycle and whether all bags clean properly.
Check that the filter housing is sealed against rain and humid air.
hook_ideas: Monsoon makes filter bags cake with dust
Damp bags, weak suction, dusty floor
product_angle: Mention filter bags and cages as seasonal items to inspect before the rains.

problem: Moisture in the compressed air line in monsoon damages the pulse valves and wets the bags.
agitation: Pulses become weak and some bags are never cleaned. The filter appears to work but suction is poor where it matters.
solution_steps: Drain the air receiver and check for water in the line.
Check the air dryer or moisture trap, if fitted.
Inspect valves and diaphragms for sticking or leakage.
hook_ideas: Wet compressed air ruins pulse cleaning
Is water in your air line hurting bags?
product_angle: Mention diaphragms and valve kits as spares worth keeping during the humid months.

problem: Dust leaks through loose bag clamps and damaged bag necks in an old filter during dry summer months.
agitation: Fine dust enters the clean air side and settles on machines and walls. Housekeeping work grows and dust looks worse near the filter outlet.
solution_steps: Inspect each bag neck and clamp for looseness or tears.
Look for dust marks on the clean air side of the tube sheet.
Replace damaged bags and fix clamps in one maintenance stop.
hook_ideas: One torn bag neck can dust the whole room
Dry summer dust finds every loose clamp
product_angle: Position bags, cages and clamps as parts to check together in a single planned stop.

problem: Pulse diaphragm valves fail one by one in a filter that has run through the busy harvest season.
agitation: Some bag rows stop cleaning properly and pressure in the system builds up. Suction at roller floor points weakens and dust collects around machines.
solution_steps: Listen for weak or missing pulses at each valve during operation.
Check the timer or controller sequence for each row.
Replace worn diaphragms in all valves of the same age together.
hook_ideas: Silent pulse valves mean dirty bags
Harvest season wears pulse diaphragms hard
product_angle: Mention a diaphragm kit as a simple, low-cost spare for the filter.

problem: The rotary airlock under the filter hopper chokes with damp dust in monsoon.
agitation: Dust builds up inside the hopper and bags start to sit in it. The airlock motor works harder and the filter has to be stopped for cleaning.
solution_steps: Check the airlock for sticky build-up and worn vane tips.
Check that the hopper walls are clear and not holding damp dust.
Check the discharge line so the dust can move away freely.
hook_ideas: Damp dust chokes the airlock, then the filter
Monsoon dust turns sticky in the hopper
product_angle: Mention airlock parts as related items to review along with bags and valves.

problem: Elevator buckets crack and wear during peak harvest-season intake when the mill runs at full load.
agitation: Broken buckets cause spillage into the boot and uneven lifting. Production stops while the elevator is opened in the busiest weeks.
solution_steps: Inspect all buckets for cracks, deformation and worn lips.
Check bucket bolts and fixing holes on the belt.
Replace worn buckets in sets and keep spare buckets ready.
hook_ideas: Harvest peak is when buckets break
Cracked buckets stop the whole mill
product_angle: Mention buckets and fixing bolts as spares to keep before the busy season.

problem: The elevator belt slips on the head pulley in humid monsoon weather.
agitation: Lifting becomes uneven and the boot starts to fill up. The operator tightens the belt again and again, which stretches it further.
solution_steps: Check belt tension and tracking at the head and boot pulleys.
Check the pulley lagging or surface for wear and damp film.
Replace the belt if stretch or damage is found along its length.
hook_ideas: A slipping elevator belt is a warning sign
Monsoon slip is stretching your elevator belt
product_angle: Mention belts and fastening items as part of a pre-monsoon elevator check.

problem: Damp stock builds up in the elevator boot in monsoon and chokes the elevator.
agitation: The motor trips and the line backs up behind the elevator. Clearing the boot wastes production time and often damages the buckets.
solution_steps: Check the boot for packed stock and clean it at each stop.
Check the inspection door seals so humid air stays out.
Check that the feed rate to the elevator is steady.
hook_ideas: Damp stock chokes elevator boots
One choked boot can halt the whole line
product_angle: Mention buckets and belts as parts that suffer when the boot chokes repeatedly.

problem: Screw conveyor flights and troughs in an older mill are worn thin and flour leaks at the joints.
agitation: Material carries over slowly and builds up in the trough. Leakage creates dust and housekeeping problems near the conveyor.
solution_steps: Inspect the flight edges and trough for wear and gaps.
Check the hanger bearings and end seals.
Plan replacement of flights during a scheduled stop.
hook_ideas: Worn flights leave flour behind
Old conveyors leak flour at every joint
product_angle: Mention conveyor flights and hanger parts as a planned replacement item for old lines.

problem: Bucket fixing bolts loosen over long summer running hours and buckets start to tilt on the belt.
agitation: Tilted buckets scrape the casing and spill stock. The belt gets damaged and the noise from the elevator gets worse.
solution_steps: Check all bucket bolts for tightness at each planned stop.
Look for elongated holes in the belt or bucket.
Replace worn fasteners with the correct type rather than any available bolt.
hook_ideas: Loose bolts turn buckets into scrap
Long summer hours loosen every elevator bolt
product_angle: Mention bucket bolts as a small item that protects the belt and buckets.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: Roll corrugations wear down faster during the heavy harvest-season grinding period and the break rolls stop opening the grain properly.
agitation: Bran gets cut up and the flour speck level rises. The miller compensates with roll gap changes, which only hides the real problem.
solution_steps: Check the roll surface for worn corrugations at regular intervals.
Compare the break release with earlier readings.
Plan roll re-corrugation before the wear becomes severe.
hook_ideas: Worn corrugations show up in your flour
Harvest load is hard on break rolls
product_angle: Mention that wear parts and roll care should be planned before the heavy intake season.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: Roll scrapers and brushes are worn and stock clings to the roll surface in humid weather.
agitation: Stock wraps around the roll and the feed to the next stage becomes irregular. Roll surfaces get damaged and flour quality varies.
solution_steps: Check scraper blade contact and wear along the whole roll length.
Check brush condition on smooth rolls.
Replace scrapers and brushes as a matched set on each machine.
hook_ideas: Worn scrapers let stock cling to rolls
Humid days expose weak roll scrapers
product_angle: Mention scrapers and brushes as regular consumable parts to keep on the shelf.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: Feed rolls and feed gates are worn and stock spreads unevenly along the roll length.
agitation: One side of the roll wears faster than the other. Flour quality changes along the roll and the miller chases the problem with adjustments.
solution_steps: Check the feed roll and feed gate for wear and uneven gaps.
Check that the stock spreads across the full roll width.
Replace worn feed parts before regrinding the main rolls.
hook_ideas: Uneven feed wears rolls on one side
Fix the feed before you blame the rolls
product_angle: Mention feed system parts as a low-cost step that protects expensive rolls.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: The roll gap adjusting mechanism in an old mill has worn parts and the setting does not hold.
agitation: Gap drifts during running and flour streams change through the shift. Operators need to reset the machine often and trust in the settings is lost.
solution_steps: Check the adjusting screws, handwheels and locks for play.
Check that both ends of the roll move together.
Replace worn adjusting parts and recheck the gap after running.
hook_ideas: A roll gap that will not hold costs quality
Old adjusters let your settings drift
product_angle: Mention adjusting parts as part of an old-mill overhaul list.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: A small mill delays smooth roll regrinding and the roll surface becomes glazed and uneven.
agitation: Reduction rolls stop working well and flour looks dull and uneven. The mill keeps running because stopping for roll service is hard to schedule.
solution_steps: Check smooth roll surface finish and the diameter along the length.
Plan roll service in a slow period rather than waiting for failure.
Keep a spare roll or schedule service in advance if possible.
hook_ideas: Glazed rolls give dull, uneven flour
Plan roll service before the busy season
product_angle: Mention roll care planning as part of seasonal maintenance support.

problem: V-belts on the roller mill drive slip in monsoon humidity and the roll speed drops.
agitation: Grinding becomes uneven and the belts heat up and glaze. A slipping drive wastes power and the motor works harder for the same output.
solution_steps: Check belt tension and look for glazed or cracked surfaces.
Check that pulleys are aligned and the grooves are clean.
Replace the whole belt set together, never a single belt.
hook_ideas: Belt slip is stealing your roll speed
Replace V-belts as a matched set
product_angle: Mention belt sets as an essential spare, especially before the humid season.

problem: Rubber inserts in couplings harden in summer heat and start to crack.
agitation: Vibration and noise increase and the shaft and bearings take the shock. A small coupling failure can stop a big machine.
solution_steps: Inspect the inserts for cracks, hardening and wear.
Check shaft alignment between motor and machine.
Replace worn inserts in all similar couplings together.
hook_ideas: Cracked coupling inserts shake the whole drive
Summer heat hardens rubber coupling parts
product_angle: Mention coupling inserts as a cheap, quick spare that avoids long breakdowns.

problem: Bearings run hot in the summer because grease is old or the wrong type is used.
agitation: Heat damages the bearing and the housing and the failure can come without warning. A bearing breakdown in peak season stops the line at the worst time.
solution_steps: Check bearing temperature by touch or thermometer on a regular routine.
Check the grease type, quantity and relubrication schedule.
Check for dust entering through damaged seals.
hook_ideas: Hot bearings give warnings before they fail
Wrong grease is a hidden bearing killer
product_angle: Mention that bearings and seals should be matched to the machine and kept as critical spares.

problem: Pulley grooves in an old mill are worn and new belts wear out quickly.
agitation: New belts sit deep in worn grooves and slip or fail early. The mill keeps buying belts without fixing the real cause.
solution_steps: Inspect the groove shape and depth on each pulley.
Check pulley alignment and belt seating.
Replace worn pulleys together with the belt set.
hook_ideas: New belts on old pulleys fail early
Worn grooves destroy belts quietly
product_angle: Mention pulleys as the part to check whenever belts keep failing.

problem: Chains and sprockets on conveyors and elevator drives stretch and wear unevenly after long running hours.
agitation: The chain jumps teeth and the drive becomes noisy. A failed chain halts the line and can damage the shaft.
solution_steps: Check chain stretch and sprocket tooth shape.
Check chain lubrication and the guard condition.
Replace the chain and sprockets as a pair.
hook_ideas: Stretched chains damage new sprockets
Replace chain and sprocket as a pair
product_angle: Mention chain and sprocket sets as planned replacement items, not emergency buys.

problem: Magnet bars are covered with dust and iron fines during harvest-season intake and no longer catch new metal.
agitation: Metal pieces pass through the magnet and reach the first break rolls. Roll surfaces get damaged and flour quality is at risk.
solution_steps: Clean the magnet surface at fixed intervals and record it.
Check that the magnet is still holding iron pieces firmly.
Check that the grain flow passes close to the magnet surface.
hook_ideas: A dirty magnet stops protecting your rolls
Clean magnets on a schedule, not by chance
product_angle: Mention that magnet bars need regular cleaning and checking to stay useful.

problem: The magnet is fitted where grain falls too fast and in a thick stream, so metal slips past.
agitation: Metal that should be caught reaches the rolls and sifters. The mill thinks it has protection while the position makes it weak.
solution_steps: Check the magnet location and the thickness of the grain stream.
Check whether a chute or spreader can slow and thin the flow.
Check that the magnet cleans easily and is not skipped by operators.
hook_ideas: A badly placed magnet only looks protective
Thick grain flow lets metal slip past
product_angle: Mention that magnet type and position should suit the chute and material flow.

problem: New-crop wheat in the harvest season arrives with nails, wire pieces and small metal from field and handling.
agitation: One piece of metal can damage a roll surface in seconds. A damaged roll means a long stop and flour quality problems for days.
solution_steps: Check that magnets are placed before the first break stage.
Check the intake area for metal pieces during each shift.
Keep a record of the foreign matter found on each magnet.
hook_ideas: Harvest wheat brings metal you cannot see
One nail can ruin a roll surface
product_angle: Mention intake magnets as an inexpensive layer of protection for the rolls.

problem: Damp flour dust cakes on magnet surfaces in monsoon and forms a crust.
agitation: The crust keeps iron particles from reaching the magnet surface. Operators think the magnet is working while it is actually blocked.
solution_steps: Check the magnet surface for a damp or hardened layer.
Increase the cleaning frequency during humid weather.
Make sure the magnet housing is dry and sealed.
hook_ideas: Monsoon crust blocks your magnet
Damp dust hides your magnet's real condition
product_angle: Mention that magnets need an adjusted cleaning routine in the rainy months.

problem: A buyer or auditor asks the mill for records of foreign matter control, but the mill has only informal habits.
agitation: The mill cannot show that magnets are checked and cleaned. Trust with a customer weakens when proof is missing.
solution_steps: Make a simple log of magnet cleaning time, person and findings.
Mark all magnet locations on the flow sheet.
Check the customer or audit requirement before setting your routine.
hook_ideas: Can you prove your magnets are checked?
Auditors ask for records, not intentions
product_angle: Mention magnets as one visible part of a documented foreign matter control routine.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: Drum sieve perforations clog with damp mud and dust from wet wheat in monsoon.
agitation: Throughput falls and dirt moves on into the cleaning section. The line slows down while the intake fills.
solution_steps: Check the sheet surface for blocked holes and clean them.
Check the brush or cleaning mechanism of the drum sieve.
Check the incoming grain moisture and dirt level.
hook_ideas: Wet wheat blocks your drum sieve holes
Monsoon mud slows the whole intake
product_angle: Mention that a properly sized drum sieve helps with dirty, damp intake.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: Perforated sheets are worn after heavy harvest intake and the holes have become too large.
agitation: Stones and large impurities pass through the openings. The downstream machines have to do work they were never meant to do.
solution_steps: Inspect the sheet for worn, enlarged or torn holes.
Compare the sheet with the original perforation requirement.
Replace worn sheets and keep a spare set ready.
hook_ideas: Worn sheet holes let stones through
Check your sheets after peak harvest intake
product_angle: Mention perforated sheets as a wear part that should be inspected after every season.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: The wire mesh in the cleaning section does not suit the size and shape of the new crop grain.
agitation: Good grain is lost with the rejects or impurities stay in the stream. The cleaning section is blamed when only the mesh needs a change.
solution_steps: Check a sample of the new crop grain against the current mesh size.
Check the reject stream for good grain loss.
Choose the mesh type and opening based on the actual grain.
hook_ideas: New crop grain may need a new mesh
Wrong mesh sends good wheat to the rejects
product_angle: Mention that mesh selection should follow the grain actually being received that season.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: Harvest wheat arrives with straw, chaff and husk that the current pre-cleaning does not remove.
agitation: Light material blocks the aspiration and the feed to later machines. Dust rises and the cleaning section works harder than it should.
solution_steps: Check what the reject stream actually contains.
Check the sieve cleaner, aspiration and sheet condition.
Check whether the pre-cleaner capacity matches the intake.
hook_ideas: Harvest straw overloads the cleaning section
Pre-clean first, mill better later
product_angle: Mention a pre-cleaner as the first filter against harvest-season straw and chaff.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: A small mill sends grain straight from intake to the cleaning section with no pre-cleaning step.
agitation: The main cleaning machines wear faster and clog often. Impurities that should be removed early travel deeper into the mill.
solution_steps: Check what is removed at the intake and what reaches the cleaning machines.
Check how often the cleaning machines need to be stopped and cleaned.
Discuss pre-cleaning options suited to the mill layout and intake rate.
hook_ideas: No pre-cleaner means harder work downstream
Small mills also need a first cleaning step
product_angle: Mention a simple pre-cleaning step as a way to protect the rest of the cleaning section.

problem: Moisture readings of wheat samples change because samples are left open in humid monsoon air.
agitation: The mill gets different readings for the same lot. Wrong tempering decisions follow and the flour quality drifts.
solution_steps: Store samples in closed containers immediately after drawing.
Use a consistent sampling and testing routine.
Check the moisture tester against a known reference regularly.
hook_ideas: Open samples give you wrong moisture readings
Monsoon air changes your lab results
product_angle: Mention that reliable lab tools and a simple sampling routine support better tempering decisions.

problem: New-crop wheat from different sources is blended without testing and flour behaviour changes from day to day.
agitation: Dough and chapati results vary and customers complain. The mill cannot explain the change because no record exists.
solution_steps: Test each incoming lot for basic parameters before blending.
Record the results next to the lot and the blend ratio used.
Compare the flour results with the blend to find patterns.
hook_ideas: Untested blends make unstable flour
Test new-crop lots before they hit the mill
product_angle: Mention that simple lab checks help the mill control blends in harvest season.

problem: A small mill judges flour quality only by colour and touch and does not test ash content.
agitation: Quality claims cannot be backed up when a buyer asks. Decisions about extraction rates are guesses rather than measurements.
solution_steps: Check which flour parameters your buyers or the rules ask for.
Set up a simple regular testing routine for those parameters.
Verify the current standards and limits from official sources.
hook_ideas: Colour alone cannot prove flour quality
Do you know your flour's ash content?
product_angle: Mention lab equipment as a way to move from judging by eye to measuring.

problem: Lab test sieves used for flour granulation checks are worn or damaged and give misleading results.
agitation: The mill thinks the flour granulation is fine while the real product is different. Plansifter changes are made on wrong information.
solution_steps: Inspect the lab sieves for damage, stretch and clogging.
Clean sieves gently and store them protected from dust and damp.
Replace worn test sieves before using the results to adjust production.
hook_ideas: A damaged test sieve gives wrong answers
Check your lab sieves before the plansifter
product_angle: Mention test sieves as small lab items that affect big production decisions.

problem: Lab balance and drying oven readings drift in the hot summer lab room and nobody checks them.
agitation: Test results become unreliable without anyone noticing. The mill makes process decisions based on numbers it cannot trust.
solution_steps: Check the lab balance and oven against a known reference.
Keep the lab instruments away from heat, dust and direct sunlight.
Make a simple calibration and checking schedule.
hook_ideas: Summer heat can quietly spoil lab readings
Who checks your lab instruments?
product_angle: Mention that lab instruments need care and checking to stay trustworthy.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: A critical part fails at harvest peak and the mill has no spare in stock.
agitation: The mill stops at the time when grain arrives and demand is highest. Waiting for a part costs far more than the part itself.
solution_steps: List the parts that would stop the mill if they failed.
Keep a minimum stock of those parts before the season starts.
Review the list after each season using actual failure records.
hook_ideas: Peak season is the worst time to wait
Stock the critical spares before harvest
product_angle: Mention helping the mill build a critical spares list before the season begins.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: The mill has no pre-monsoon checklist and finds problems only after damp weather causes failures.
agitation: Several small problems appear together and each one stops production. The team fixes issues in a hurry with whatever is at hand.
solution_steps: Make a short list of items to check before the rains.
Include belts, sieve cloth, filter bags, sleeves and sealing points.
Schedule the check during a planned stop and order any missing items.
hook_ideas: A pre-monsoon checklist saves emergency stops
Check before the rains, not during them
product_angle: Mention a seasonal checklist and matching spares as a practical service offer.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: A small mill adds capacity by buying one new machine without checking how it fits the rest of the flow.
agitation: The new machine overloads the next stage or waits for stock. Money is spent but the mill output does not improve as expected.
solution_steps: Map the current flow and find the real bottleneck.
Check how the new machine will match the stages before and after it.
Discuss the layout and capacity needs before deciding.
hook_ideas: One new machine rarely fixes a mill
Find the bottleneck before buying equipment
product_angle: Offer help in matching machine choice to the existing flow and mill goals.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: An older mill needs spares for machines whose drawings and part details are lost.
agitation: Ordering takes long because nobody is sure about size or fit. Wrong parts arrive and the machine remains down.
solution_steps: Note the machine name, details on the nameplate and the part position.
Take clear photos and measurements, or send the old part as a sample.
Create a simple spares record so the next order is faster.
hook_ideas: Lost drawings should not mean long downtime
Photos and samples make spare ordering easier
product_angle: Mention that the team can help identify parts from samples, photos and machine details.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: In the busy season, the mill cannot get a technician to check a problem quickly.
agitation: The team tries to fix a fault without full knowledge and may make it worse. The longer the delay, the more production and grain handling is disturbed.
solution_steps: Keep contact details of the service support for each machine.
Prepare a clear description, photos and a short video of the problem.
Plan a routine service visit before the season to avoid last-minute calls.
hook_ideas: Book service before the harvest rush starts
Clear photos help a faster service response
product_angle: Mention a pre-season service visit as a simple way to avoid peak-time breakdowns.

problem: On cold winter mornings, moisture condenses inside the plansifter at start-up and fine stock forms lumps on the sieves.
agitation: Lumps ride on the cloth and block the openings. The first hours of every shift give poor sifting and the operator makes unnecessary changes elsewhere.
solution_steps: Check the inside of the sifter and the sieve cloth for damp patches at start-up.
Run the machine empty for a short time before feeding stock.
Check that sieve cleaners are in place and moving freely.
hook_ideas: Cold starts leave damp lumps on sieves
Winter mornings can blind your plansifter
product_angle: Mention sieve cleaners and spare cloth as simple items that help during cold-weather start-ups.

problem: Under festival-season order pressure, the plansifter runs at a heavy feed and sieve cloth tears near the frame edges.
agitation: Torn cloth lets coarse particles into finer flour. Quality complaints arrive just when the mill is busiest and demand is highest.
solution_steps: Inspect cloth edges and corners at every frame for early tears or loose fixing.
Check that the feed to the sifter is steady and not overloaded.
Keep ready-to-fit cloth of the right grade for the common positions.
hook_ideas: Festival rush tears sieve cloth at the edges
Heavy feed shows up first in your sieves
product_angle: Suggest keeping spare cloth for high-wear positions before the festival rush.

problem: Hanging rods and suspension parts of an old plansifter are worn and the sifter no longer moves in a smooth, even circle.
agitation: Stock travels unevenly across the sieves and one side carries more load. Noise and vibration rise and nearby parts loosen faster.
solution_steps: Check the suspension rods, ends and fixing points for wear or cracks.
Check that the sifter body hangs level and moves evenly.
Replace worn suspension parts in matched sets.
hook_ideas: A tired plansifter hanger spoils the whole motion
Even sifting starts with sound suspension parts
product_angle: Mention suspension parts as items to check during an old-mill overhaul.

problem: Sieve cleaner balls in the plansifter have worn into uneven sizes and some no longer clean the cloth.
agitation: Parts of the sieve stay blinded while other parts are clean. Sifting capacity drops slowly and nobody can say when it started.
solution_steps: Open a sieve section and compare the cleaner balls for size and shape.
Check that cleaners bounce freely under the cloth.
Replace worn cleaners as a full set for each section.
hook_ideas: Worn cleaner balls silently blind your sieves
Small cleaners, big effect on sifting capacity
product_angle: Position cleaners as a low-cost consumable with a fixed replacement routine.

problem: Re-clothing a plansifter takes a long time because no ready-clothed spare frames are kept.
agitation: A whole section stays idle during the work and the mill either stops or runs in a weak condition. Rushed fitting often leaves uneven tension.
solution_steps: Count the frames and sections that have wear risk.
Prepare a few spare frames with correct cloth for quick swapping.
Note the cloth grade and position for every frame.
hook_ideas: Spare frames turn long stops into quick swaps
Re-clothing should not stop your mill for hours
product_angle: Mention ready-to-fit spare frames and cloth as a smart stock for busy mills.

problem: After a change in wheat type, the old purifier cloth combination no longer suits the stock coming to it.
agitation: Good semolina goes with the bran and bran specks stay in the clean stock. The miller blames the wheat when the cloth is the real mismatch.
solution_steps: Check the stock on each deck and compare it with the intended cloth grading.
Look at where good particles are being lost or impurities remain.
Review the cloth combination before changing air or tilt again.
hook_ideas: New wheat may need a new purifier cloth setup
Wrong cloth grading hides good semolina in bran
product_angle: Mention that cloth selection can be reviewed whenever the wheat type changes.

problem: The feed inlet and distributor of the purifier are worn and stock lands on one side of the deck.
agitation: One side of the cloth is overloaded and the other side is almost empty. Separation is poor even though the air looks correct.
solution_steps: Check the inlet, flaps and distributor for wear, gaps or build-up.
Watch how the stock spreads across the full deck width.
Replace or repair worn feed parts before changing settings.
hook_ideas: Uneven feed ruins purifier separation
Check the inlet before touching the air
product_angle: Mention inlet and feed parts as often-forgotten items in a purifier check.

problem: Operators patch torn purifier cloth with tape during a busy festival run and leave it for weeks.
agitation: Tape holes block air and tear further. Stock bypasses around the patch and the machine loses its purpose.
solution_steps: Mark every patched area and check the cloth around it.
Plan a proper cloth change for the next stop.
Keep a spare cloth set so patching is not the only choice.
hook_ideas: Tape patches are not a purifier repair
Temporary fixes become permanent quality loss
product_angle: Suggest a spare cloth set so staff are never forced to patch.

problem: A large mill with many purifiers has cloth of different ages on each machine and the streams do not match.
agitation: Two machines on the same job give different results. Operators set each purifier differently and the flow sheet is no longer followed.
solution_steps: List the cloth type and installation date for each purifier.
Compare the stock quality from each machine side by side.
Set a standard replacement routine for all machines.
hook_ideas: Same job, different cloth age, different results
Standardise your purifier cloth replacement
product_angle: Mention planned replacement sets for mills that run several purifiers.

problem: Sight windows and cover gaskets on the purifier are broken, so air leaks and the stock bed cannot be seen clearly.
agitation: Air pattern changes and the operator cannot judge the bed behaviour. Dust escapes around the cover and cleaning time rises.
solution_steps: Check cover seals, gaskets and sight windows for damage.
Check for dust marks around the edges while running.
Replace damaged seals and clean the windows for a clear view.
hook_ideas: A leaking purifier cover changes the air pattern
You cannot adjust what you cannot see
product_angle: Mention seals and sight windows as small parts that make adjustment easier.

problem: On cold winter nights, moisture condenses inside the jet filter housing and the dust on the bags turns sticky.
agitation: Pulse cleaning cannot shake off the damp dust. Suction falls in the morning and dust escapes at machine points.
solution_steps: Check the inside of the housing and bags for dampness in the morning.
Check the housing joints and doors for leaks that let cold air in.
Check that the filter runs briefly after the last stock is cleared.
hook_ideas: Cold nights make filter dust sticky
Winter condensation hurts jet filter cleaning
product_angle: Mention bags and door seals as parts to check in the cold season.

problem: Bag cages in an old jet filter are rusted and bent and the bags wear through where they touch the cage.
agitation: Holes appear at the same places each time. Dust passes through and bags need replacing again and again.
solution_steps: Pull a few bags and cages and look for rust, bends and sharp points.
Check that bags sit smoothly on straight cages.
Replace bent cages when changing bags.
hook_ideas: Bent cages quietly cut your new bags
Change cages, not just bags
product_angle: Position cages as the part to check every time bags are replaced.

problem: The pressure gauge on the jet filter is broken, so nobody knows when the bags are blocked.
agitation: Bags are changed only when dust is visible in the room. By then suction has been poor for a long time and machines have suffered.
solution_steps: Check that the gauge or indicator shows a reading and responds to change.
Note the normal reading and record it daily.
Investigate whenever the reading moves away from normal.
hook_ideas: No gauge means you fly blind on dust control
A pressure reading tells you when bags need help
product_angle: Mention that a working gauge and simple records help plan bag replacement.

problem: A new machine was connected to an old jet filter line and suction at the old points dropped.
agitation: Dust appears at machines that were clean earlier. The mill blames the fan, but the real change was the added load on the system.
solution_steps: List every point connected to the filter and compare with the original plan.
Check the duct and damper settings at each point.
Check filter bags and cleaning before any change to fan or ducts.
hook_ideas: New machine, old filter, weak suction
Adding a machine can starve your dust control
product_angle: Offer to review the dust control setup whenever a machine is added to the mill.

problem: Mixed bag fabrics are fitted in the same jet filter because the original type was not available.
agitation: Some bags clean well and others stay blocked. Cleaning looks uneven and the cause is difficult to see from outside.
solution_steps: Open the filter and check whether all bags are of the same type.
Note any bag that looks different in dust build-up.
Replace mixed bags with a matching set at the next stop.
hook_ideas: Mixed bags clean unevenly and wear unevenly
Keep one bag type across the whole filter
product_angle: Mention keeping a matching bag set in stock so substitutes are never needed.

problem: The belt joint of a bucket elevator opens up under heavy load and the belt starts to fail near the splice.
agitation: The belt can separate in running and drop buckets into the boot. A long stop and big clean-up follow.
solution_steps: Inspect the joint, lacing or splice for loose or worn parts.
Check that the belt ends are square and properly joined.
Plan belt joint replacement during a scheduled stop.
hook_ideas: A weak belt joint can drop the whole elevator
Check the splice before it checks you
product_angle: Mention belt joining parts as items to keep along with spare belting.

problem: In a newly installed mill, the elevator belt keeps running to one side and rubs the casing.
agitation: The belt edge wears and the casing gets damaged. Operators keep adjusting without finding the root cause.
solution_steps: Check the alignment of the head and boot pulley shafts.
Check that the casing is straight and not twisted.
Adjust tracking in small steps while watching the belt.
hook_ideas: A new elevator belt should not wander
Misaligned pulleys wear belts from day one
product_angle: Mention belts and pulleys as parts to check together when tracking problems persist.

problem: Replacement buckets of a different shape are mixed with the original buckets on the same belt.
agitation: Buckets fill and discharge unevenly. The elevator lifts less than expected and spillage starts at the head.
solution_steps: Compare all buckets for size, depth and shape.
Check that bucket spacing and fixing match the belt.
Replace mismatched buckets with a matching set.
hook_ideas: Mixed buckets give uneven lifting
One odd bucket can upset the whole elevator
product_angle: Suggest ordering buckets by matching the existing type, with a sample if needed.

problem: The wheat intake belt conveyor spills grain at the transfer point and the belt edges are worn.
agitation: Grain on the floor means loss and extra cleaning. Dust rises and the belt wears faster on the side that rubs.
solution_steps: Check the belt alignment and the rollers under it.
Check the chute, skirt rubbers and transfer points for gaps.
Replace worn skirt rubbers and damaged belt sections.
hook_ideas: Spilled grain at transfers is wasted effort
Worn skirts and rollers waste grain daily
product_angle: Mention skirt rubbers and belt parts as intake items that need regular checking.

problem: An elevator has no choke or speed sensor and belt slip goes unnoticed until the boot is full.
agitation: The motor trips and the boot has to be dug out by hand. Buckets and the belt get damaged during clearing.
solution_steps: Check whether any alarm or sensor exists on the elevator.
Check the belt speed with a simple method during running.
Discuss adding a sensor with your electrician or supplier.
hook_ideas: A slipping elevator should warn you early
Catch belt slip before the boot chokes
product_angle: Mention that protection and monitoring parts can be discussed together with belts and buckets.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: Dust seals at the roll ends are worn and flour works its way toward the roll bearings.
agitation: Bearings pick up dust and run hotter. The roll end becomes dirty and a bearing failure can stop the whole passage.
solution_steps: Check roll end seals for wear, cracks and flour leakage.
Look around the bearing housing for flour build-up.
Replace worn seals at the next planned stop.
hook_ideas: Worn roll seals let flour into bearings
A cheap seal protects an expensive bearing
product_angle: Mention roll end seals as small parts that protect bearings and rolls.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: Smooth rolls have worn unevenly along their length and the middle is thinner than the ends.
agitation: Flour is thicker at the roll ends and thinner in the middle. Streams change and the miller keeps changing the gap without success.
solution_steps: Check the roll diameter at several points along the length.
Check the feed spread and roll bearings for causes of uneven wear.
Plan regrinding and fix the cause at the same time.
hook_ideas: Uneven roll wear shows up as uneven flour
Check roll diameter along the full length
product_angle: Mention roll care as a planned service rather than an emergency job.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: The roll disengage mechanism is worn and the rolls touch each other when the feed stops.
agitation: Rolls run metal on metal and the surface is damaged. Noise rises and flour quality drops after every short stop.
solution_steps: Check the engage and disengage movement for play or sticking.
Check the feed sensor or stop control, if fitted.
Replace worn linkage parts before roll damage becomes serious.
hook_ideas: Empty rolls should never touch
Worn disengage parts damage expensive rolls
product_angle: Mention disengage parts as wear items that protect the rolls.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: Gaskets and covers around the roll aspiration are damaged and dust leaks out of the roller mill.
agitation: The mill floor stays dusty and air flow through the machine changes. Stock sticks inside and roll temperature is harder to control.
solution_steps: Check the covers, gaskets and aspiration connections for gaps.
Check the air flow at each roller mill after fixing leaks.
Replace damaged seals as part of routine servicing.
hook_ideas: Leaky roll covers spoil air flow and floor
Fix roller mill gaskets before chasing dust
product_angle: Mention gaskets and covers as simple items for a roller mill service kit.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: After regrinding the rolls, the scrapers, gap and feed are not reset for the smaller roll diameter.
agitation: Stock clings to rolls and the first hours after regrinding give poor flour. The mill assumes the regrind did not help.
solution_steps: Check the scraper contact after every roll change.
Reset the gap and compare with earlier readings.
Record the new roll diameter for future reference.
hook_ideas: Regrinding is half the job; resetting is the rest
New roll diameter needs new scraper settings
product_angle: Mention that scrapers should be replaced or reset along with every roll service.

problem: Frequent power trips in festival-season peak load cause shock on the drive and keys and keyways wear out.
agitation: Pulleys and couplings become loose on shafts and give noise and vibration. A key failure stops a machine without warning.
solution_steps: Check keys and keyways on motors and main shafts for play.
Check that pulleys and couplings are tight on their shafts.
Replace worn keys with correct fit rather than packing them.
hook_ideas: Power trips shake loose keys and pulleys
Loose keys fail without warning
product_angle: Mention keys and fasteners as small drive parts worth keeping in stock.

problem: Taper lock bushes on pulleys loosen over time and the pulley starts to wobble.
agitation: The belt wears quickly on one side and the shaft is damaged. The wobble spreads vibration to bearings and the machine.
solution_steps: Check the bush bolts for tightness and the pulley for run-out.
Look for shaft marks or fretting under the bush.
Replace worn bushes and fit them according to the right procedure.
hook_ideas: A wobbling pulley eats belts and bearings
Check pulley bushes at every planned stop
product_angle: Mention bushes with pulleys and belts as one drive set to review together.

problem: In an older mill, the foundation has settled and bearing housings are out of alignment.
agitation: Bearings run hot and wear unevenly. Shafts bend slightly and belts or couplings fail early.
solution_steps: Check shaft alignment and look for uneven bearing wear.
Check base bolts and housing seating for looseness.
Realign and replace worn bearings together when needed.
hook_ideas: Settled foundations quietly kill bearings
Old mills need alignment checks, not only new parts
product_angle: Mention bearings and housings as parts to inspect as a set in older mills.

problem: Gearbox oil seals on conveyor or elevator drives have hardened and oil leaks near the flour stream.
agitation: Oil drips onto parts and floor and mixes with dust. The gearbox runs low on oil and wears faster.
solution_steps: Check the oil level and look for leaks around the shaft seals.
Check that the breather is clear and the oil type is correct.
Replace worn seals before the gearbox itself is damaged.
hook_ideas: A leaking gearbox seal is a small warning
Oil near flour needs fixing quickly
product_angle: Mention oil seals as low-cost spares for gearbox drives.

problem: Operators apply belt dressing or resin to slipping belts instead of finding the cause.
agitation: The slip stops for a while and then returns. Dust sticks to the belt and the real problem of tension or worn parts continues.
solution_steps: Check belt tension, pulley grooves and alignment first.
Remove old dressing and clean the belt and pulley surfaces.
Replace the belt set if it is glazed or damaged.
hook_ideas: Belt dressing hides the real problem
Fix the cause of slip, not the symptom
product_angle: Mention that a matched belt set and correct tension remove the need for dressing.

problem: A small mill has magnets only at intake and none later in the flow before the plansifter or finished flour.
agitation: Metal that enters after intake, from wear or repair work, passes straight on. Late-stage contamination is much harder to trace.
solution_steps: Mark the magnet positions on a flow diagram of the mill.
Look for stages where no magnet protects the stream.
Discuss extra magnet positions suited to the mill layout.
hook_ideas: Intake magnets alone are not enough
Where does metal enter after the intake?
product_angle: Mention adding magnets at selected later stages as a practical improvement.

problem: An old magnet has been in the mill for many years and nobody has checked whether it still holds metal.
agitation: The mill assumes protection exists while the magnet may have weakened. Metal slips past without anyone knowing.
solution_steps: Test the magnet with a small iron piece to see how firmly it holds.
Check the condition of the housing and the surface.
Replace or recharge weak magnets according to supplier advice.
hook_ideas: When did you last test your old magnet?
An old magnet may protect less than you think
product_angle: Mention a simple magnet check and replacement plan for old installations.

problem: After maintenance work, loose bolts, wire pieces and small tools are left inside machines or spouts.
agitation: These parts enter the product stream at the next start. A single bolt can hit a roll or choke a spout and cause a long stop.
solution_steps: Count tools and fasteners before and after every maintenance job.
Check the magnets after the first run following maintenance.
Make a short checklist for closing machines after service.
hook_ideas: Forgotten bolts become tomorrow's roll damage
Count your tools before closing the machine
product_angle: Mention magnets as a backup, while good maintenance habits are the first protection.

problem: New operators do not know how to clean drawer or plate magnets and often skip the job.
agitation: The magnet fills up and stops catching new metal. The log shows nothing and the first sign of trouble is damage downstream.
solution_steps: Show every new operator how the magnet is opened and cleaned.
Put a clear tag or label on each magnet with the cleaning interval.
Check the cleaning record at the end of each week.
hook_ideas: A magnet nobody cleans protects nothing
Train every new operator on magnet cleaning
product_angle: Mention that easy-to-clean magnet design helps operators keep the routine.

problem: Stones, glass and plastic pieces reach the rolls even though the mill believes its magnets are enough.
agitation: Magnets only hold iron. Other foreign matter damages rolls or ends up in the product while the mill feels safe.
solution_steps: Check what types of foreign matter are found in the rejects.
Check that destoning and sieving steps in the cleaning section work well.
Use magnets as one layer along with proper cleaning machines.
hook_ideas: Magnets catch iron, not stones or glass
One layer of protection is never enough
product_angle: Explain that magnets and cleaning machines work together as layers of protection.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: Wire mesh in the cleaning sieve has small tears that staff close with wire and clamps.
agitation: Repairs open again soon and rejects mix with good grain. The mesh becomes weaker with each patch.
solution_steps: Inspect the mesh for tears, loose edges and broken fixing.
Check the tension and frame of the sieve.
Replace the mesh instead of repeating small repairs.
hook_ideas: Patched mesh fails again and again
Replace torn mesh instead of repairing it twice
product_angle: Mention ready spare mesh so replacement is quick and repairs are not needed.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: Old stored wheat has a lot of fine dust and broken grain that fills the cleaning section sieves.
agitation: Sieve openings stay blocked and the cleaning section slows down. Throughput falls and the operator keeps stopping the line to clean.
solution_steps: Check what fills the sieve and whether it is dust, broken grain or husk.
Check the aspiration and brush action on the sieves.
Check that sheet openings are suitable for the stock being cleaned.

Stored wheat needs a different cleaning setup
product_angle: Mention that sheet choice can be reviewed when stored and fresh stock are handled differently.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: After a drive change, the drum sieve speed and slope are not right and grain runs through without proper sieving.

Check the slope and the feed rate into the drum.
Check the grain residence time by watching the stream.

Fast grain passes through without being cleaned
product_angle: Mention that drum sieve settings and drive parts should be matched properly.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: In a large mill running day and night, perforated sheets crack at the welds and supports.

Mark cracks and plan replacement before they grow.
Keep a spare set for the busiest sieves.
hook_ideas: Non-stop running cracks perforated sheets
Inspect weld lines before the sheet fails
product_angle: Position spare sheets as planned stock for mills that run round the clock.

problem: Small round weed seeds and cracked grain stay in the wheat because the hole shape does not suit the job.

Compare the hole shape and size with the unwanted material.
Discuss round or slotted holes based on what actually needs to be removed.

Check what your sieve is not removing
product_angle: Mention that hole shape and size should be chosen from a real grain sample.

problem: After rain at harvest, sprouted wheat enters the mill and flour behaves weakly in the bakery or chapati line.

Record the lot number with the flour results.

Test the lot before you blend it

problem: Flour samples are taken from one point only and do not represent the whole shift.
agitation: Lab results look fine while customers see variation. The mill loses trust in its own test results.

Draw samples in a consistent way and label them clearly.
Compare sample results over several days to see patterns.

A good test needs a good sample
product_angle: Mention sampling tools and containers as part of a simple lab routine.

problem: Granulation checks are done by hand shaking and results change from operator to operator.

Use a consistent shaking method and fixed time for each test.
Check whether a lab sieve shaker would suit your testing routine.
hook_ideas: Hand-shaken tests give hand-made results
Same sample, different operators, different numbers
product_angle: Mention a lab sieve shaker as a way to make granulation tests repeatable.

problem: A mill supplying fortified flour is asked for test records and does not know which checks are required.

solution_steps: Check the current rules and buyer requirements from official sources.
List the tests and records that are required for your product.
Set up a simple routine and record sheet for those tests.
hook_ideas: Do you know which flour tests are required?
Records matter as much as the test itself
product_angle: Mention that lab tools support the routine once the mill confirms what it must test.

problem: Wheat at the gate is accepted by eye and a quick feel, and no test weight or foreign matter check is done.
agitation: Poor lots enter the mill and the cleaning section pays the price. Price disputes with suppliers are difficult without any measurement.
solution_steps: Set a simple gate test for moisture, test weight and foreign matter.
Record results against the supplier and lot.
Use the records to decide on blending or rejection.
hook_ideas: Test the wheat at the gate, not after
Eyes alone cannot judge a wheat lot
product_angle: Mention basic gate testing tools as a practical step for every size of mill.

Make a simple list with part name, machine and quantity.
Check the store every few months and remove damaged items.

problem: A new small mill buys machines for a dream capacity and then runs them at very low load.

Discuss a flow that can grow in stages when demand rises.
Check space, power and future expansion points in the plan.

A mill that can grow in stages is safer

Compare a repair plan with a staged upgrade plan.

agitation: The benefit of the service fades and the mill thinks the repair did not work. The same fault is called in again and again.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: The festival shutdown is used only for cleaning and the mill has no proper overhaul list.

hook_ideas: Use the festival shutdown for a real overhaul

product_angle: Mention a shutdown checklist with matching spares as a practical service offer.

problem: In a large mill, wide sieve cloth sags in the middle after long running and stock piles up in the centre of the sieve.

solution_steps: Check cloth tension across the full width, not only at the edges.

Wide sieves need tension checks across the full width

problem: After a partial re-clothing, new and old sieve cloth run together in the same plansifter section.

product_angle: Suggest ordering cloth by full section so frames age evenly.

problem: Clamping bolts and hold-down parts of the sieve stack loosen and the frames rattle during running.
agitation: Frames shift and gaps open between them. Flour leaks sideways and the noise tells the operator something is wrong, but the cause is not obvious.

Replace worn clamping parts rather than reusing damaged ones.

Loose clamps open gaps between sieve frames
product_angle: Mention clamping parts and gaskets as small items that keep the stack tight.

problem: In a newly commissioned mill, sieve cloth numbers are not marked on frames and positions get mixed after the first cleaning.
agitation: Wrong cloth ends up in the wrong place and the stock splits no longer match the design. The new mill underperforms and the cause is blamed on the machines.
solution_steps: Mark every frame with its section and position as per the flow sheet.
Check the installed cloth grade against the sheet, frame by frame.
Keep a simple chart of cloth positions near the plansifter.
hook_ideas: Unmarked frames mix up your new mill's sieves
Label every sieve frame from day one
product_angle: Mention that cloth supplied with clear grade details makes position tracking easier.

problem: An older plansifter has cracks and gaps in frame corners where stock settles and cannot be cleaned out.
agitation: Old stock stays in the corners and spoils fresh flour on the next run. Cleaning takes longer and some stock is never removed.
solution_steps: Open the stack and check frame corners and joints for settled stock.
Check for cracks, loose joints and damaged edges.
Repair or replace frames that cannot be cleaned properly.
hook_ideas: Old frame corners hold stock you cannot see
Cracked frames trap old flour in the sifter
product_angle: Mention frame replacement as a practical upgrade for older sifters.

problem: Over-tempered wheat gives sticky, soft stock and the purifier sieve clogs faster than before.
agitation: Semolina clings to the cloth and the air cannot lift particles properly. Operators change tilt and air again and again while the real cause is upstream.
solution_steps: Check the tempering moisture and rest time against your usual practice.
Inspect the purifier cloth for sticky build-up and blinded areas.
Check that cleaning brushes under the deck are working.
hook_ideas: Over-tempered wheat clogs purifier cloth
Check tempering before you blame the purifier
product_angle: Mention cloth and brushes as parts to inspect whenever stock turns sticky.

problem: New purifier cloth is fitted with wrinkles and uneven tension because the fitting steps were rushed.
agitation: Wrinkles lift stock unevenly and cause air to channel through weak spots. The new cloth performs worse than the old and wears out early.
solution_steps: Check that the cloth is flat, square and evenly tight across the deck.
Check the fixing strips and edges for proper seating.
