hook_ideas: Wrinkled new cloth works worse than old cloth
Fitting matters as much as the cloth itself
product_angle: Mention that cloth supplied with correct fixing parts makes fitting easier.

problem: The deck drive or eccentric parts of an older purifier are worn and the deck knocks while running.
agitation: Stock moves unevenly and the sieve cloth tears near the frame. Noise grows and neighbouring parts loosen from the vibration.
solution_steps: Listen and feel for knocking in the drive area while running.
Check the bearings, bushes and fixing points of the drive.
Replace worn drive parts together before the cloth is damaged further.
hook_ideas: A knocking purifier deck is asking for help
Worn drive parts tear new sieve cloth
product_angle: Mention drive-side parts along with cloth when planning an old purifier overhaul.

problem: Spare purifier cloth is kept folded in a corner of the store and gets creased and dusty before use.
agitation: Creases stay in the cloth after fitting and weak lines tear early. The mill pays for a new cloth that behaves like an old one.
solution_steps: Store spare cloth flat or rolled in a clean, dry place.
Check each spare cloth for creases, damage and damp before fitting.
Label each cloth with the machine and deck position.
hook_ideas: Folded spare cloth is damaged before you fit it
Store spare purifier cloth flat and dry
product_angle: Mention that spare cloth should be ordered and stored in a way that keeps it fit for use.

problem: A small mill with one purifier has no spare set and the whole line suffers when the cloth must be changed.
agitation: The mill either runs with worn cloth or stops production while waiting. Quality drops because there is no easy way to change quickly.
solution_steps: Check the current cloth condition and expected remaining life.
Keep one ready spare set for the single purifier.
Note the cloth details and deck positions in a simple record.
hook_ideas: One purifier needs one ready spare cloth set
Small mills cannot wait for cloth to arrive
product_angle: Suggest that a small mill keep one ready cloth set as basic insurance.

problem: Dust-laden air hits the bags directly at the filter inlet and the nearest bags wear out first.
agitation: Bags near the inlet fail again and again while the others look fine. Dust leaks out and the mill keeps replacing bags without finding the pattern.
solution_steps: Check which bags wear out first and where they sit in the housing.
Check the inlet baffle or deflector for wear or damage.
Replace worn bags and repair the baffle in the same stop.
hook_ideas: Bags near the inlet always fail first
Find the pattern before you buy more bags
product_angle: Mention bags and wear-prone parts as items to review together with the inlet condition.

problem: The pulse controller of the jet filter has a fault and several valves fire together or not at all.
agitation: Some rows are over-cleaned and others are never cleaned. Bags wear in some places and block in others, and suction becomes uneven.
solution_steps: Watch and listen to the pulse order during running.
Check the controller settings and wiring connections.
Replace a faulty controller or timer and check each valve again.
hook_ideas: A faulty pulse timer ruins bags and suction
Check the order of your filter pulses
product_angle: Mention controller and valve parts as related items for a complete filter check.

problem: Compressed air pressure for the filter is low because of leaks and the compressor is shared with other uses.
agitation: Pulses are weak and bags do not clean properly. The filter looks fine from outside while dust control slowly gets worse.
solution_steps: Check the air pressure at the filter during pulsing.
Walk the air line and listen for leaks at joints and fittings.
Check whether other users are drawing air at the same time.
hook_ideas: Weak air means weak pulses and dirty bags
Air leaks quietly spoil your filter cleaning
product_angle: Mention valve diaphragms and fittings as parts that matter when air pressure is limited.

problem: Dust builds up on the fan impeller of the filter system and the suction slowly falls.
agitation: The fan vibrates and the bearings run harder. Dust appears at machine points even though the bags are clean.
solution_steps: Open the fan inspection door and check for dust build-up on the blades.
Check the fan vibration and bearing condition.
Clean the impeller and check the filter bags for dust passing through.
hook_ideas: A dusty fan impeller weakens suction slowly
Weak suction is not always a bag problem
product_angle: Mention that fan and bearing checks can be added to a service visit along with filter parts.

problem: Dust settles inside long ducts of an old mill because clean-out doors are missing or sealed shut.
agitation: Air flow drops and some machines lose suction. Staff try to fix it by opening dampers further, which pulls less air from the other points.
solution_steps: Mark the duct runs and check for horizontal sections where dust can settle.
Check that inspection and clean-out doors are present and open easily.
Clean the ducts at a planned stop and then recheck suction at each point.
hook_ideas: Settled dust in ducts starves your machines of air
Old ducts need clean-out doors and a schedule
product_angle: Mention that duct checks fit naturally alongside bag and valve checks on the filter.

problem: The head pulley lagging of a bucket elevator is worn smooth and the belt slips even at correct tension.
agitation: Lifting capacity falls and operators keep tightening the belt. The belt stretches and the boot fills slowly over the shift.
solution_steps: Check the pulley surface or lagging for wear and polish.
Check the belt tension before and after cleaning the pulley.
Replace worn lagging instead of tightening the belt further.
hook_ideas: Smooth worn lagging makes belts slip
Tighter belts do not fix a worn pulley
product_angle: Mention pulley lagging and belt as parts to check together when slip is a repeated issue.

problem: Elevator casing joints and inspection doors leak flour dust along the full height of the leg.
agitation: Dust settles on floors and railings and the machine area is hard to keep clean. Stock lost at the joints is small but constant.
solution_steps: Look along the casing for dust marks at joints and doors.
Check the door seals and bolts for damage or looseness.
Replace worn seals and tighten all joints in one stop.
hook_ideas: Leaky elevator joints make dust on every floor
Seal the leg before you clean the floor again
product_angle: Mention door seals and casing parts as small items that improve housekeeping.

problem: Stock falls back from the buckets at the head and returns to the boot instead of going to the discharge.
agitation: Lifting seems normal but the output is weak. The boot keeps filling and the motor draws power for work that does not reach the next machine.
solution_steps: Check belt speed and compare it with the design speed.
Check the bucket shape and the head pulley condition.
Check that the discharge area is clear and the casing is not worn.
hook_ideas: Falling-back stock makes the elevator work twice
Check bucket shape and speed at the head
product_angle: Mention that matching buckets and belt speed is part of selecting conveying parts.

problem: Idler rollers on the intake belt conveyor have seized and the belt drags over them.
agitation: The belt wears through on the underside and the drive motor works harder. A worn belt can fail suddenly during a busy intake.
solution_steps: Spin each roller by hand and mark the ones that do not turn.
Check the belt underside for flat wear marks.
Replace seized rollers and check belt alignment again.
hook_ideas: One seized roller can wear through a belt
Check every idler before the busy intake
product_angle: Mention rollers and belts as parts to keep in the intake spares list.

problem: End plates and shaft seals of a flour screw conveyor leak and flour packs around the bearing.
agitation: The packed flour makes the bearing run hot and sticks to the shaft. Cleaning takes time and a bearing failure can stop the line.
solution_steps: Check the end plate seals for leaks and wear.
Check the bearing area for flour build-up and heat.
Replace worn seals and clean the bearing area at each stop.
hook_ideas: Leaking conveyor seals pack flour into bearings
A small seal leak can cook a bearing
product_angle: Mention shaft seals and bearings as paired items for flour conveyors.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: A hard object has dented the roll surface and every rotation leaves a mark in the stock.
agitation: The dented spot damages the opposite roll slowly and the flour shows uneven streaks. The mill keeps running because the damage looks small.
solution_steps: Stop and inspect the roll surface for dents, chips and marks.
Check the opposite roll for matching damage.
Plan regrinding or replacement before the damage spreads.
hook_ideas: A small dent on a roll becomes a big problem
Inspect rolls after any metal or stone event
product_angle: Mention that roll service and spare rolls can be planned before damage becomes serious.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: After a pulley change on the roller mill drive, the speed difference between fast and slow rolls is no longer correct.
agitation: The roll action changes and flour streams look different from before. The mill suspects the wheat while the drive ratio has been altered.
solution_steps: Check the pulley and gear sizes against the original drive details.
Check the roll speeds with a simple speed measuring method.
Restore the correct ratio before changing gap or feed settings.
hook_ideas: Wrong pulley changes the roll speed ratio
Check roll speed before blaming the wheat
product_angle: Mention that pulleys and gears should be matched to the original drive details.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: The stock level sensor or feed flap in the roller mill is coated with flour and gives wrong signals.
agitation: The feed runs too much or too little and the roll gap opens and closes at the wrong time. Flour quality varies without a clear cause.
solution_steps: Clean the sensor or flap and check if the movement is free.
Check the wiring and mounting for damage or looseness.
Observe the feed behaviour for a full shift after cleaning.
hook_ideas: A dirty feed sensor makes rolls behave badly
Clean the small parts before changing big settings
product_angle: Mention feed control parts as small items that deserve a place in the spares list.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: Only one passage of an old mill gets new rolls and the rest keep old, worn rolls.
agitation: The new passage works well and pushes more load downstream. The worn rolls cannot keep up and the benefit of the new rolls is lost.
solution_steps: Compare the roll condition of the passages before and after.
Check the load and stock quality going to the next passage.
Plan roll renewal in logical groups instead of single passages.
hook_ideas: New rolls on one passage may overload the next
Plan roll renewal across the whole flow
product_angle: Mention planning roll service by passage groups, not one at a time.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: Roller mill doors and cover latches are broken and operators leave the doors partly open during running.
agitation: Dust and flour escape and room air enters the roll chamber. Roll temperature and stock behaviour change and housekeeping suffers.
solution_steps: Check all doors, latches and hinges on each roller mill.
Check the door seals for damage and gaps.
Replace broken latches and make closing a shift routine.
hook_ideas: A broken latch lets dust out and air in
Closed doors keep roll conditions steady
product_angle: Mention latches and seals as inexpensive items for a roller mill service kit.

problem: On a multi-belt drive, one belt is slack while the others are tight and the load is not shared.
agitation: The tight belts overheat and wear quickly. The slack belt hangs and flaps, and the whole set needs to be replaced sooner than expected.
solution_steps: Compare the tension of all belts on the drive.
Check that all belts are the same type and age.
Replace the whole set together and retension after a short run.
hook_ideas: One slack belt overloads the rest of the set
Belts must share the load equally
product_angle: Mention matched belt sets as the right way to buy and replace belts.

problem: Different staff grease the bearings with different greases and in different amounts.
agitation: Mixed greases break down and over-greasing makes bearings hot. Some bearings get nothing for weeks and then too much at once.
solution_steps: Decide one grease type and one quantity for each bearing group.
Mark the grease points and assign one person per area.
Keep a simple greasing record for each machine.
hook_ideas: Mixed greases and over-greasing heat bearings
One grease, one routine, one responsible person
product_angle: Mention that bearing and seal choice should go together with a clear greasing routine.

problem: After a motor is replaced, the coupling alignment is not checked and the new motor bearing runs hot.
agitation: Vibration travels into the machine and shaft seals leak. The new motor gets blamed while the alignment was never set properly.
solution_steps: Check shaft alignment between the motor and the driven machine.
Check the coupling parts for wear after the first days of running.
Recheck bearing temperature and vibration after a week.
hook_ideas: A new motor still needs a proper alignment
Check coupling alignment after every motor change
product_angle: Mention couplings and alignment checks as a standard step after motor replacement.

problem: A replacement motor has a different speed and the machine pulley is not changed to match.
agitation: The machine runs faster or slower than designed. Stock behaviour changes and the mill struggles to find the cause.
solution_steps: Check the motor speed on the nameplate against the original motor.
Check the pulley sizes needed to bring the machine to design speed.
Measure the machine speed after the change and record it.
hook_ideas: A different motor speed needs a different pulley
Match the motor and pulley, not just the power
product_angle: Mention that pulley sizing can be worked out from motor and machine details.

problem: Bearings on the plansifter drive fail often because the machine runs slightly out of balance.
agitation: Vibration shortens bearing life and the housings loosen. Each failure stops the plansifter and the rest of the line waits.
solution_steps: Check the balance weights and the hanging points of the plansifter.
Check bearing housings and base bolts for looseness.
Replace bearings together with worn seals and recheck vibration.
hook_ideas: An unbalanced plansifter eats its own bearings
Fix the balance, then replace the bearing
product_angle: Mention bearings and seals for the plansifter drive as critical spares to keep.

problem: A magnet in the finished flour line shows fine iron dust every week and nobody checks where it comes from.
agitation: The mill treats it as normal and never looks for the worn part. The source keeps wearing and the iron dust stays in the flour path.
solution_steps: Collect and note what the magnet catches in each week.
Look for worn metal parts upstream such as scrapers, screws or flights.
Inspect and replace the suspected worn part at the next stop.
hook_ideas: Iron dust on the magnet is a clue, not normal
Trace the iron back to the worn part
product_angle: Mention that magnet findings help point to worn parts that need replacing.

problem: A newly installed mill sheds fine metal particles from new parts during the first weeks of running.
agitation: Particles enter the product stream before the machines settle in. The mill is new but the first flour already carries a risk.
solution_steps: Plan more frequent magnet cleaning in the first weeks.
Record what each magnet catches during commissioning.
Check that all magnets are clean before every start-up.
hook_ideas: New machines shed metal in their first weeks
Clean magnets more often during commissioning
product_angle: Mention magnets as part of the commissioning checklist for a new mill.

problem: The housing cover of a spout magnet is damaged and flour leaks out around the magnet door.
agitation: Flour dust spreads near the magnet and operators stop cleaning it because the area is messy. A skipped magnet protects nothing.
solution_steps: Check the door, hinges and seals of each magnet housing.
Check that the magnet can be opened and closed easily.
Repair or replace the housing parts before the next shift.
hook_ideas: A messy magnet housing gets skipped by staff
Easy-to-open magnets get cleaned more often
product_angle: Mention that magnet housing design affects how well cleaning is followed.

problem: A magnet sits in a flour spout where flour bridges and the stream does not touch the magnet surface.
agitation: Iron particles pass in the centre of the flow and never meet the magnet. The mill believes the line is protected when it is not.
solution_steps: Watch how the flour flows through the spout at the magnet position.
Check whether the stream touches the magnet surface properly.
Discuss a better magnet position or type with your supplier.
hook_ideas: A magnet the flour never touches catches nothing
Check where your flour actually flows
product_angle: Mention choosing magnet type and position to suit the spout and flow.

problem: Operators open and clean magnets while the line is running, and stock spills and mixes with the rejects.
agitation: Cleaning is rushed and the iron is left behind. Spilled stock makes the area dirty and some operators avoid the job.
solution_steps: Check which magnets are cleaned during running and which at stops.
Check whether the magnet design allows safe and quick cleaning.
Set a simple cleaning method for each magnet and train the operators.
hook_ideas: Rushed magnet cleaning leaves iron behind
Make magnet cleaning quick, safe and clean
product_angle: Mention easy-clean magnet types for lines where stopping is difficult.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: The deck sheet of the destoner is blocked in places and stones are not separated evenly.
agitation: Stones travel with the wheat to the rolls in some lots. The destoner looks busy but does not give the protection the mill expects.
solution_steps: Check the deck sheet for blocked holes and worn areas.
Check the air flow and the stock bed on the deck.
Replace the damaged deck sheet and review the settings after.
hook_ideas: A blocked destoner deck lets stones reach the rolls
Check the deck sheet before the stones check your rolls
product_angle: Mention deck sheets as a wear and clog item for the destoner.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: The aspirator in the cleaning section pulls good light grain into the reject along with the husk.
agitation: Good wheat is lost and the reject stream looks heavy. The mill blames the grain quality while the air setting is too strong.
solution_steps: Check the reject stream for good grain.
Check the air setting and the feed spread across the aspirator.
Adjust in small steps and compare the reject after each change.
hook_ideas: Too much air sends good wheat to the reject
Check your reject stream for good grain
product_angle: Mention that cleaning machine settings should be matched to the grain being handled.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: The dampening screw does not mix water evenly and the wheat enters the tempering bin with wet and dry grains together.
agitation: Tempering becomes uneven and the roll work changes through the day. The cleaning section output looks good but milling is not stable.
solution_steps: Check the water flow and the spread along the screw.
Check the screw flights and casing for wear or build-up.
Compare the grain moisture before and after the dampener.
hook_ideas: Uneven dampening makes uneven milling
Check water mixing before the tempering bin
product_angle: Mention that the dampening step is part of the cleaning section review.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: A replaced perforated sheet is fitted facing the wrong direction and grain does not pass the holes properly.
agitation: Throughput drops after the change and the operator thinks the new sheet is faulty. Staff lose time re-fitting during production.
solution_steps: Check the hole direction on the sheet before fitting.
Compare the new sheet with the old one on size, shape and direction.
Fit and test at low feed before returning to full load.
hook_ideas: A sheet fitted the wrong way blocks the flow
Check hole direction before you tighten the sheet
product_angle: Mention that sheets supplied with clear fitting details avoid such mistakes.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: Rubber cleaning balls under the grain separator sieve are hard, cracked and no longer keep the holes open.
agitation: The sieve slowly blocks and the separation gets worse. Operators stop to clean by hand and lose cleaning capacity.
solution_steps: Check the rubber balls for hardness, cracks and size.
Check that they move freely under the sieve.
Replace the full set and note the date of change.
hook_ideas: Hard rubber balls stop cleaning your sieve
Small cleaning balls keep big sieves working
product_angle: Mention cleaning balls as a low-cost item that supports the sheets and mesh.

problem: Gluten washing results change from day to day because water temperature and washing time are not controlled.
agitation: The mill cannot compare lots fairly and decisions on blending become guesses. Customers see changes the lab did not predict.
solution_steps: Fix a standard sample weight, washing time and water condition.
Record the method on a card kept next to the equipment.
Compare results from two operators on the same sample.
hook_ideas: Uncontrolled washing gives uncontrolled gluten results
Fix your method before you trust your numbers
product_angle: Mention lab equipment together with a written standard method for repeatable results.

problem: The test weight apparatus is used for years without checking and nobody knows if it still gives correct readings.
agitation: Wheat lots are accepted or priced on a number that may be wrong. Disputes with suppliers cannot be settled with confidence.
solution_steps: Check the apparatus for damage, dents and worn parts.
Compare the readings with a reference or a second instrument.
Set a regular check date and record it.
hook_ideas: Is your test weight reading still correct?
Check the instrument before you reject a lot
product_angle: Mention that gate test instruments should be checked and replaced when worn.

problem: Ash test crucibles are chipped and the lab furnace is used without a fixed routine.
agitation: Ash results vary for the same flour and the mill cannot trust its extraction decisions. Time is spent repeating tests.
solution_steps: Check crucibles for chips, cracks and residue.
Follow a fixed time and temperature routine for each test.
Record the results and compare with earlier readings.
hook_ideas: Chipped crucibles give doubtful ash results
Ash tests need a fixed routine
product_angle: Mention crucibles and furnace care as part of a reliable ash testing routine.

problem: After a customer complaint, the mill finds no retained flour sample from that day to compare.
agitation: The mill cannot check what went out and cannot prove or disprove the complaint. The customer loses trust while the cause stays unknown.
solution_steps: Keep a labelled retained sample from each day or lot.
Store samples in clean, closed containers in a dry place.
Keep a simple register with date, shift and lot details.
hook_ideas: No retained sample means no answer to a complaint
Keep a labelled sample from every day
product_angle: Mention sample containers and a simple register as part of a basic lab setup.

problem: Bran speck and flour colour are judged by eye in different lights and the opinion changes from person to person.
agitation: One shift passes the flour and the next shift rejects the same flour. Staff lose confidence and rolls and sieves are changed without a clear reason.
solution_steps: Use one fixed place with the same light for every colour check.
Compare against a kept reference sample each time.
Check whether a simple colour or speck test method suits your flour.
hook_ideas: Different lights give different opinions on colour
Judge flour colour in one fixed place
product_angle: Mention simple lab tools that make colour and speck checks more repeatable.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: A mill buys spare parts from an unknown local source and the parts wear out much earlier than expected.
agitation: The mill pays again and again for the same part and each failure stops the line. Nobody can say whether the part or the machine is the problem.
solution_steps: Note the part, the supplier and the date of fitting and failure.
Compare the failed part with the original for material and finish.
Choose a supplier who can match the part to the machine.
hook_ideas: A cheap spare that fails early is costly
Record how long each spare actually lasts
product_angle: Mention that parts matched to the machine and kept in records give better planning.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: A mill using many different wheat sources wants one machine setup to suit all of them.
agitation: The flow works for some lots and struggles with others. The miller keeps changing settings and quality swings with each new purchase.
solution_steps: List the wheat types and sources the mill really buys.
Note which lots cause trouble and in which section.
Discuss flexible settings or added machines for the weak area.
hook_ideas: Many wheat sources need a flexible mill flow
Match your machines to the wheat you really buy
product_angle: Offer to review the wheat mix and suggest where the flow needs flexibility.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: A mill plans to add a roller mill but the power supply and transformer load have not been checked.
agitation: The new machine starts but the supply is weak and trips often. The mill pays for the machine and then loses time on power problems.
solution_steps: Check the present electrical load and the supply limit.
Check space, foundation and layout for the new machine.
Discuss the plan with your supplier and electrician before ordering.
hook_ideas: Check your power supply before buying a machine
A new machine also needs power, space and layout
product_angle: Offer to discuss layout and power needs together with the machine choice.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: A mid-sized mill calls for service only after a breakdown and has no regular service visits.
agitation: Small faults grow into big ones and each repair is urgent and rushed. The mill never gets a clear picture of its machine condition.
solution_steps: List machines that have had repeated faults in the last year.
Plan a regular service visit for the most critical machines.
Keep a short report of each visit and follow up on the findings.
hook_ideas: Regular service is calmer than emergency repair
Small faults found early stay small
product_angle: Mention regular service visits with a written report as a practical support.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: The spares store is full of slow-moving items while fast-wearing parts are missing when needed.
agitation: Money sits on the shelf and the mill still stops for a small part. Staff lose trust in the spares list and buy in a hurry.
solution_steps: Review the last year's failures and list the parts used most often.
Move stock levels toward fast-wearing and critical parts.
Review the list every season and remove items never used.
hook_ideas: Stock what fails, not what looks safe
Review your spares list after every season
product_angle: Offer help to build a spares list based on actual failure records.

problem: After a sudden power cut, the plansifter stops with stock on the sieves and restarts under a heavy, uneven load.
agitation: Settled stock presses on the cloth and the first minutes of running give poor sifting. Cloth can tear or blind and the streams take long to settle again.
solution_steps: Check the sieve cloth for tears or pressed stock after every sudden stop.
Check that sieve cleaners moved freely and were not stuck by settled flour.
Let the sifter run a short time to clear stock before feeding at full load.
hook_ideas: Power cuts leave stock pressed on your sieves
Check sieve cloth after every sudden stop
product_angle: Mention spare sieve cloth and cleaners as items to keep for areas with frequent power cuts.

problem: Staff clean blinded sieve cloth with sharp tools or wire brushes at shift end.
agitation: Tiny cuts and stretched wires appear in the cloth. Flour passes where it should not and the cloth wears out much sooner than expected.
solution_steps: Check the cloth for scratches, cuts and uneven wire spacing.
Replace sharp tools with a soft brush or the cleaning method the supplier advises.
Train cleaning staff and mark which sections were cleaned each shift.
hook_ideas: Sharp tools shorten the life of sieve cloth
Clean sieves gently or replace them early
product_angle: Mention that a correct cleaning method and spare cloth go together in sieve care.

problem: Outlet spouts and collecting trays of the plansifter choke with flour lumps and stock backs up inside the sifter.
agitation: Backed-up stock mixes between channels and loads the sieves from below. The operator sees poor sifting but the choke is hidden from view.
solution_steps: Check each outlet spout and tray for packed flour at every stop.
Check the sleeves and connecting parts for kinks or narrow bends.
Clean the chokes and check whether damp stock is causing the lumps.
hook_ideas: Hidden spout chokes back up your plansifter
Poor sifting may start below the sieve
product_angle: Mention sleeves and connecting parts as items to check when stock backs up.

problem: When the mill changes its product mix, the same sieve cloth set is kept for every product.
agitation: Flour granulation shifts and the mill struggles to hold its target. The miller keeps changing rolls while the cloth no longer suits the job.
solution_steps: List the products made and the target granulation for each one.
Compare the installed cloth grades with what each product needs.
Discuss a cloth set or spare set for the second product.
hook_ideas: New product mix may need a new sieve cloth set
Same cloth for every product limits your flour
product_angle: Mention that cloth grades can be reviewed whenever the product mix changes.

problem: Flour residue stays in plansifter corners and gaps in a warm mill and insects start to appear.
agitation: Old residue mixes into fresh stock on the next run. The mill spends more time on cleaning and still finds the problem returning.
solution_steps: Open the sections and check frame edges, corners and gasket grooves for old residue.
Set a regular deep-cleaning day for the plansifter.
Replace damaged gaskets and frames that cannot be cleaned properly.
hook_ideas: Old flour in sifter corners invites insects
Deep-clean your plansifter on a fixed schedule
product_angle: Mention gaskets and frames as parts that make deep cleaning possible.

problem: The aspiration duct of the purifier is partly choked with settled dust and air is pulled unevenly.
agitation: The stock bed lifts in some places and sinks in others. The operator changes the air damper again and again without fixing the real choke.
solution_steps: Check the duct and connection to the purifier for packed dust.
Check the damper movement and the air flow after cleaning.
Compare the stock bed behaviour before and after the clean-out.
hook_ideas: A choked duct changes your purifier air
Clean the duct before you move the damper
product_angle: Mention that cloth and seal checks fit well with a duct and air check.

problem: A mill running day and night wears out purifier cloth in a short time and replacement is always urgent.
agitation: The mill replaces cloth in a hurry, often with whatever is available. Separation changes after every emergency change.
solution_steps: Record how long each cloth lasts under non-stop running.
Plan the replacement date before the cloth reaches its limit.
Keep a ready set of the correct cloth for each deck.
hook_ideas: Non-stop mills need planned purifier cloth changes
Do not wait for the cloth to fail
product_angle: Suggest ready spare cloth sets scheduled by running hours for round-the-clock mills.

problem: Air dampers and adjusting handles of an old purifier are rusted and stuck in one position.
agitation: The operator cannot set air for different stock and the purifier works the same way for every lot. Separation suffers when the wheat changes.
solution_steps: Check each damper and handle for rust, play and smooth movement.
Free or replace stuck parts and mark the settings clearly.
Record the air setting that works for each wheat type.
hook_ideas: Stuck air dampers make every wheat run the same
You cannot tune what will not move
product_angle: Mention adjusting parts as items for an old purifier overhaul.

problem: Break roll settings were opened up and the purifier suddenly gets more bran-rich stock than before.
agitation: The cloth blinds sooner and the bed becomes heavy. Operators blame the purifier while the change came from the rolls.
solution_steps: Compare the stock reaching the purifier with the earlier normal stock.
Check the cloth and brushes for blinding from the heavier load.
Review the break roll change together with the purifier settings.
hook_ideas: Roll changes upstream can overload your purifier
Check what reaches the purifier before adjusting it
product_angle: Mention cloth and brushes as parts that show the effect of upstream changes.

problem: A new miller copies purifier settings from another mill and uses them without checking the local stock.
agitation: The same settings give different results because the wheat, cloth and machine age are different. Time is lost while the miller wonders why.
solution_steps: Check the cloth type and condition against the other mill's setup.
Start from a basic setting and observe the stock on each deck.
Write down the final settings with the wheat type used.
hook_ideas: Another mill's purifier settings may not suit yours
Set your purifier by your stock, not by copy
product_angle: Mention that correct cloth for your stock makes settings easier to find.

problem: New staff fit replacement filter bags without proper seating on the tube sheet and the bag necks.
agitation: Dust leaks past the neck and reaches the clean side. The new bags look fine but dust control is no better than before.
solution_steps: Check each new bag neck and clamp after fitting.
Look for dust marks on the clean side after the first day of running.
Show new staff the correct fitting method with an example.
hook_ideas: New bags badly fitted still leak dust
Check every bag neck after a bag change
product_angle: Mention bags supplied with matching clamps and cages for simple fitting.

problem: Dust bridges inside the filter hopper and does not fall to the discharge point.
agitation: Dust level rises and covers the lower bags. Cleaning becomes weak and the filter has to be stopped to empty the hopper by hand.
solution_steps: Check the hopper walls for packed dust and the angle of the slope.
Check the discharge valve and the line after it for blockage.
Clean the hopper regularly and note how fast it fills.
hook_ideas: Bridged dust in the hopper buries your bags
Empty hoppers keep filters working properly
product_angle: Mention hopper and discharge parts as items to review along with bags.

problem: False air enters through worn door gaskets and loose covers on the filter housing.
agitation: Suction at machine points falls even though the fan runs normally. Staff blame the bags while air is leaking into the filter instead of coming from the machines.
solution_steps: Check the gaskets and latches on all filter doors and covers.
Listen for hissing at joints while the fan runs.
Replace worn gaskets and recheck suction at the machines.
hook_ideas: Door leaks steal suction from your machines
False air makes the fan work for nothing
product_angle: Mention door gaskets as inexpensive parts that restore suction.

problem: The fan belts of the filter system slip and the air flow is lower than before.
agitation: Dust escapes at machine points and the fan heats up. Staff clean bags without result because the real issue is the drive.
solution_steps: Check belt tension and condition on the fan drive.
Check the pulley grooves and alignment.
Replace the whole belt set if glazed or worn and retension after a short run.
hook_ideas: A slipping fan belt looks like a bag problem
Check the fan drive before changing bags
product_angle: Mention a matched belt set and pulleys as part of a fan drive check.

problem: The pulse interval of the filter was set once at installation and was never adjusted to the real dust load.
agitation: Bags are cleaned too often or too little. Wear rises in one case and blocking in the other, and bag life becomes short.
solution_steps: Check the present pulse interval and compare it with the mill load.
Watch the pressure reading before and after pulsing.
Adjust in small steps and record the results for each change.
hook_ideas: Pulse settings need to follow your actual dust load
Too many pulses wear bags, too few block them
product_angle: Mention bags and valves as items to monitor when the cleaning cycle is tuned.

problem: Take-up screws at the elevator boot are seized and the belt cannot be tensioned properly.
agitation: The belt stays loose and slips. Operators pull the belt by other means and the buckets and casing get damaged.
solution_steps: Check the take-up screws and slides for rust and seizing.
Free and grease the parts and check if both sides move equally.
Replace damaged take-up parts at the next planned stop.
hook_ideas: Seized take-up screws leave you with a loose belt
Free the boot adjusters before the belt slips
product_angle: Mention take-up parts along with belts and buckets in an elevator check.

problem: The elevator has no anti-runback arrangement and the belt rolls backward when the motor stops.
agitation: Stock from the legs falls into the boot and chokes it. The next start is heavy and the motor trips again.
solution_steps: Check whether a backstop or holding device is fitted and working.
Check the boot after each stop for fallen stock.
Discuss a suitable holding arrangement with your supplier.
hook_ideas: Stopped elevators that roll back choke the boot
Backward belt movement causes the next start trouble
product_angle: Mention that elevator protection parts can be discussed along with buckets and belts.

problem: Oil leaking from a gearbox drips on the elevator belt and the belt surface turns slippery.
agitation: The belt slips on the pulley and the oil soaks into the rubber. Flour sticks to the oily patches and the belt weakens.
solution_steps: Check the gearbox seals and find the source of the oil.
Clean the belt and pulley surfaces and check for rubber damage.
Replace the belt if the rubber is swollen or soft.
hook_ideas: Oil on the belt makes it slip and weaken
Fix the leak first, then clean the belt
product_angle: Mention that belt replacement should follow the removal of the oil source.

problem: Flights of a chain or drag conveyor are worn and flour is left behind in the trough.
agitation: Old flour stays in the trough and mixes with the next lot. Cleaning takes longer and the chain draws more power.
solution_steps: Check the flights, chain links and trough for wear.
Check the chain tension and the sprocket tooth condition.
Replace worn flights and chain parts in matched sections.
hook_ideas: Worn flights leave old flour in the trough
Old flour mixing in is a conveyor problem too
product_angle: Mention flights and chain parts as planned replacement items for older conveyors.

problem: After capacity was raised, the old elevator belt is used with the same buckets and the lifting is not enough.
agitation: The boot overfills and the motor trips. The mill adds a bigger machine upstream while the elevator limits the whole line.
solution_steps: Compare the elevator lifting ability with the new flow rate.
Check the belt strength, bucket size and belt speed together.
Discuss options with your supplier before changing the other machines.
hook_ideas: More capacity needs an elevator that can lift it
Your elevator may be the real bottleneck
product_angle: Offer to review elevator capacity whenever the mill flow is increased.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: During a long monsoon shutdown, rust forms on the roll surfaces and the first flour after restart shows dark specks.
agitation: Rust spoils the first stock and rolls may need extra work before running well. The mill loses time while it sorts out the cause.
solution_steps: Check the roll surface for rust before restart.
Plan how rolls will be protected during long stops.
Run and check the first stock separately before it joins the main flow.
hook_ideas: Rusty rolls spoil your first flour after restart
Protect rolls before a long monsoon stop
product_angle: Mention roll care and protection as part of shutdown planning.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: Roll temperature rises after hours of running and flour from the roller mill feels warm and slightly sticky.
agitation: Stock clings to the rolls and scrapers and sifting suffers. The miller opens the gap, which only hides the heat problem.
solution_steps: Check the roll aspiration and cover seals for air flow problems.
Check roll bearings and belts for extra heat or friction.
Compare stock temperature at the start and end of a shift.
hook_ideas: Warm rolls make sticky stock and weak sifting
Check roll air flow before changing the gap
product_angle: Mention seals and aspiration parts as simple items that affect roll temperature.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: The pressure springs or loading parts of the roller mill have weakened and the rolls separate under load.
agitation: Roll contact changes with the stock load and flour quality swings. The miller adjusts the gap again and again without success.
solution_steps: Check the springs or loading parts for fatigue, rust and damage.
Check that both roll ends hold pressure equally.
Replace weak parts as a matched set on the same machine.
hook_ideas: Tired springs let rolls drift under load
Roll pressure should be equal at both ends
product_angle: Mention loading parts as items to keep in a roller mill service kit.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: The roll gap scale or indicator is worn and the readings differ from the real gap.
agitation: Operators trust the scale and set the gap wrongly. Two mills of the same type give different results with the same reading.
solution_steps: Check the scale and pointer for wear, play and damage.
Check the real gap with a simple method and compare it with the reading.
Replace or reset the indicator and note the correction.
hook_ideas: A worn gap scale gives you the wrong gap
Check the real gap, not only the dial
product_angle: Mention indicator parts as small items worth checking in older mills.

category: Roller mill accessories and wear parts
problem: Rolls have been reground so many times that they are close to the minimum usable diameter.
agitation: Further regrinding is not possible and the mill is forced into a sudden roll change. Flour quality and production suffer while waiting for new rolls.
solution_steps: Measure the present roll diameter and compare it with the original.
Estimate how many more regrinds are possible.
Plan the replacement and order before the limit is reached.
hook_ideas: Know how many regrinds your rolls have left
Order new rolls before the old ones run out
product_angle: Mention roll replacement planning based on measured diameter.

problem: Belt guards are missing or loose on roller mill drives and dust collects on belts and pulleys.
agitation: Dust makes belts slip and wear. Loose guards rattle and staff remove them, which also creates a safety risk for the operators.
solution_steps: Check that guards are present, firm and in good condition on every drive.
Clean dust from belts and pulleys during each planned stop.
Replace damaged guards and make fitting them a routine.
hook_ideas: Missing guards cost belts and safety
Dust on belts starts with a missing guard
product_angle: Mention guards as part of a complete drive check along with belts and pulleys.

problem: A repaired pulley is fitted again without balancing and the drive vibrates at running speed.
agitation: Vibration shakes bearings and belts and the noise grows over time. The mill replaces belts again and again without finding the cause.
solution_steps: Check the pulley for run-out and balance before refitting.
Check the bush and key fit on the shaft.
Replace a badly worn or damaged pulley rather than repeat repairs.
hook_ideas: An unbalanced pulley shakes the whole drive
Repeated pulley repairs cost more than a new pulley
product_angle: Mention that pulleys can be replaced as matched parts with bushes and belts.

problem: A rigid coupling is used on a drive that needs some flexibility and shaft damage starts early.
agitation: Small misalignments pass straight into the shafts and bearings. The mill loses bearings and seals more often than it should.
solution_steps: Check the coupling type against the drive and the machine needs.
Check shaft alignment and bearing condition on both machines.
Discuss a suitable flexible coupling with your supplier.
hook_ideas: Wrong coupling type damages shafts and bearings
A flexible coupling forgives small misalignment
product_angle: Mention that coupling type should be chosen from the drive details.

problem: Bearings are fitted by hammering on the outer ring and fail much earlier than expected.
agitation: Hidden damage shortens bearing life and the failure appears after a few weeks. The mill thinks the bearing quality is poor.
solution_steps: Check the fitting method used by the maintenance staff.
Use proper fitting tools or heating methods as advised for bearings.
Check the shaft and housing for wear before fitting a new bearing.
hook_ideas: Hammered bearings fail before their time
How a bearing is fitted decides how long it lasts
product_angle: Mention bearings along with fitting guidance as part of spares support.

problem: Spare V-belts are hung on a nail in a hot store and stretch out of shape before they are used.
agitation: New belts do not run true and wear quickly in the drive. The mill pays for spares that behave like old belts.
solution_steps: Store belts flat or loosely coiled in a cool, dry place.
Check each belt for cracks, stretch and damage before fitting.
Label belt sets by machine so the right set is used.
hook_ideas: Belts hung on nails stretch before use
Store spare belts flat and away from heat
product_angle: Mention matched belt sets supplied and stored per machine.

problem: Wheat arrives in bags with stitching wire, hooks and loose metal and the mill has only one weak magnet at intake.
agitation: Metal reaches the cleaning machines and wears sheets and screws. The first line of defence is thin while the risk is high.
solution_steps: Check what metal pieces are found on intake and in rejects.
Check the number and position of magnets before the cleaning section.
Discuss a stronger or extra magnet at the intake point.
hook_ideas: Bagged wheat brings wire and hooks into the mill
One weak intake magnet is not enough
product_angle: Mention a stronger intake magnet as a first layer of protection.

problem: A buyer finds a metal particle in a flour lot and the mill cannot show where in the process it could have entered.
agitation: Trust with the buyer suffers and the mill checks every machine without a clear plan. The same problem can return without being found.
solution_steps: Mark all magnet locations and cleaning records on the flow sheet.
Check which stages have no protection at all.
Inspect machines for worn or loose metal parts that could shed particles.
hook_ideas: Metal complaint? Start with your magnet map
Know where metal can enter, and where it is caught
product_angle: Mention reviewing magnet positions as a practical response to a complaint.

problem: A magnet is fitted close to a hot motor or heated area and loses holding strength over time.
agitation: The mill thinks the magnet is working but it holds less each month. Iron particles pass without being noticed.
solution_steps: Check the surrounding temperature at the magnet position.
Test the holding strength with a small iron piece.
Move or replace the magnet if heat is the likely cause.
hook_ideas: Heat can quietly weaken a magnet
Test your magnet where the heat is
product_angle: Mention choosing the magnet type to suit the working conditions.

problem: A magnet is placed in a pneumatic or aspiration line where air carries the material at high speed.
agitation: Particles pass the magnet too fast to be caught. The mill believes it has protection but the design does not allow it.
solution_steps: Check the speed and path of the material at the magnet position.
Check whether the flow can be slowed or guided toward the magnet.
Discuss a more suitable position in the gravity flow.
hook_ideas: Fast air flow can carry metal past a magnet
A magnet needs slow, close contact to work
product_angle: Mention that magnets work best where material flow can be slowed and guided.

problem: Magnets in the bran and by-product lines are ignored because the mill thinks only the flour line needs protection.
agitation: Metal in the by-product stream reaches the buyer and damages the mill's name. The loss is small until a complaint arrives.
solution_steps: List all outgoing streams and check which have magnets.
Add magnets to by-product lines where metal can pass.
Include these magnets in the daily cleaning routine.
hook_ideas: Bran lines also need magnets
Every outgoing stream deserves protection
product_angle: Mention magnets for by-product lines as an easy extension of the routine.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: The scourer screen is worn and wheat skin and dirt are not removed properly before milling.
agitation: Dirt stays in the groove of the grain and reaches the rolls. Bran specks rise and the cleaning section looks busy without doing its job.
solution_steps: Inspect the scourer screen for worn or enlarged openings.
Check the beaters and the gap between beaters and screen.
Replace the worn screen and compare the cleaned grain before and after.
hook_ideas: A worn scourer screen leaves dirt on the grain
Check the screen before blaming the cleaning flow
product_angle: Mention scourer screens as wear items that need regular inspection.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: The intake hopper grid is broken or missing and large objects enter the cleaning line.
agitation: Stones, wood and rope pieces choke the elevators and spouts. A long stop is needed to clear them and machines are damaged.
solution_steps: Check the intake grid for gaps, bends and missing bars.
Check the spacing of the grid against what you want to stop.
Repair or replace the grid and make checking it a daily task.
hook_ideas: A broken intake grid lets big objects in
Protect the line from the very first step
product_angle: Mention grids and heavy mesh as simple items that protect the whole line.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: Thin perforated sheets bend under heavy grain load and the holes distort.
agitation: Bent sheets change the flow of grain and some holes close up. Cleaning becomes uneven and the sheets are replaced often.
solution_steps: Check sheets for bends, waves and distorted holes.
Check the supports under the sheet for gaps or wear.
Compare the sheet thickness with the load it carries.
hook_ideas: Thin sheets bend under heavy grain loads
Sheet strength should match the real load
product_angle: Mention that sheet thickness and support should suit the load.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: Rejects from the cleaning section are collected together and nobody checks what they contain.
agitation: Good grain may be lost and the mill never knows. Problems in the sieves or aspirator stay hidden for months.
solution_steps: Take a sample from each reject stream once per shift.
Separate and look at the good grain, husk, dust and stones.
Adjust sieve, air or feed based on what you find.
hook_ideas: Your rejects tell you what your cleaning misses
Look inside the reject bin once a shift
product_angle: Mention that reject checks help to review the cleaning machines objectively.

category: Cleaning section, drum sieve / pre-cleaner, perforated sheets and wire mesh
problem: Spare wire mesh is stored in a rolled bundle and arrives with kinks and wavy lines when used.
agitation: Wavy mesh does not sit flat on the frame and the grain passes unevenly. Gaps appear at the edges and cleaning becomes poor.
solution_steps: Store mesh flat or in a gentle roll in a dry place.
Check each mesh for kinks and damage before fitting.
Fit with even tension and test at low load first.
hook_ideas: Kinked mesh never sits flat on the frame
Store spare mesh flat and dry
product_angle: Mention ready-to-fit mesh supplied cut to the frame size.

problem: Wheat samples for moisture testing are ground for different times and the results do not match.
agitation: The same lot shows different moisture on different days. Tempering decisions follow numbers that cannot be trusted.
solution_steps: Fix one grinding time and one sample quantity for the test.
Check that the grinder is clean before each sample.
Compare two readings of the same sample and note the difference.
hook_ideas: Different grinding times, different moisture readings
Make your moisture test repeatable first
product_angle: Mention lab grinders and moisture testers as a pair that needs a standard method.

problem: A mill buys a new wheat lot on the supplier's word and finds the flour weak only after milling the whole lot.
agitation: The mill has to blend heavily and the flour quality drops. A small test before buying would have shown the problem.
solution_steps: Take a representative sample from the lot before purchase.
Run basic lab tests and a small trial if possible.
Decide on buying and blending using the results.
hook_ideas: Test a wheat lot before you buy the whole lot
A small trial can save a big mistake
product_angle: Mention that a small lab mill and basic tests help in buying decisions.

problem: An export buyer asks for specific test reports and the mill does not know which methods to follow.
agitation: The mill risks losing the order while it searches for methods and equipment. Reports in the wrong format are rejected.
solution_steps: Get the exact parameters and methods the buyer requires in writing.
Check the official method for each parameter.
Check whether your lab equipment suits those methods.
hook_ideas: Ask the buyer which test methods they require
Match your lab to the buyer's report needs
product_angle: Mention that lab equipment can be reviewed once the required methods are confirmed.

problem: Lab results are written on loose paper and nobody can compare this month with the last month.
agitation: Slow changes in wheat or flour are missed. The mill reacts only after a complaint arrives.
solution_steps: Make a single register or sheet for all daily tests.
Record the lot, date, shift and the person who tested.
Review the record weekly and mark any change.
hook_ideas: Loose papers hide slow changes in quality
One register shows trends you cannot see otherwise
product_angle: Mention that good records make the most of every lab instrument.

problem: The lab sieve test uses too much or too little sample and the result changes every time.
agitation: Granulation numbers jump from test to test and the plansifter is adjusted by guesswork. The lab loses credibility with the miller.
solution_steps: Fix the sample weight for each type of test.
Use the same shaking time and clean the sieves after each test.
Repeat a test on the same sample to check consistency.
hook_ideas: The wrong sample size gives the wrong granulation
Fix your sample weight for every sieve test
product_angle: Mention lab sieves and balances as a pair for repeatable granulation tests.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: A mill buys a second-hand roller mill at a low price and finds many worn parts only after installation.
agitation: The savings disappear as parts are replaced one by one. The mill also finds that some spares are hard to match.
solution_steps: Inspect rolls, bearings, drives and frames before buying.
List the parts likely to need replacement and check availability.
Compare the total cost of repair with other options before deciding.
hook_ideas: A cheap second-hand mill can hide big repair needs
Inspect the wear parts before you buy
product_angle: Offer to help review a second-hand machine and its likely spares needs.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: Skilled operators leave and new staff do not know the machines, so small faults grow.
agitation: Settings are lost and the mill depends on one or two people. Each change of staff brings a period of poor quality.
solution_steps: Write simple operating and checking steps for each machine area.
Pair new staff with experienced ones for the first weeks.
Ask the supplier for a short training or demonstration for the team.
hook_ideas: When operators leave, settings leave with them
Write down how your machines are run
product_angle: Mention short operator training and checklists as part of after-sales support.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: A new mill is handed over without a clear list of settings, spares and checks to follow.
agitation: The owner does not know what to keep in stock or what to check. Early problems become expensive because there is no reference.
solution_steps: Ask for the flow sheet, settings and part details at handover.
Make a first-year spares list with the supplier.
Plan an early service visit after the first months of running.
hook_ideas: A new mill needs a handover file, not just keys
Ask for settings and a spares list at handover
product_angle: Mention a handover file and first-year spares list as part of every new mill.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: To meet demand, the mill extends running hours and cuts the weekly maintenance stop.
agitation: Wear parts reach their limit sooner and failures come together. The extra hours are lost in breakdowns.
solution_steps: Check which parts wear fastest at the new running hours.
Keep a short fixed maintenance window even in busy weeks.
Increase spares stock for parts that now wear faster.
hook_ideas: Extra running hours need extra maintenance
Skipping the weekly stop costs more later
product_angle: Mention reviewing the spares list when running hours increase.

category: Spares planning, machine selection and after-sales service
problem: A mill in a remote area waits many days for each spare part and has no plan for delivery time.
agitation: Small parts cause long stops because transport takes time. The mill loses grain handling days that cannot be recovered.
solution_steps: Note the delivery time for each critical part to your location.
Keep stock of parts whose delivery time is long.
Order routine parts in a planned lot instead of one by one.
hook_ideas: Remote mills must plan spares by delivery time
Long transport time needs a bigger spares shelf
product_angle: Mention planned spares kits sent in advance for mills far from the supplier.
